why: The arithmetic is trivial and the error directions are not. What is shared here is only what is pure in both copies: how far apart two points are, and whether a coordinate is worth comparing against at all. The verdict itself — inside, outside, no_location, not_checked — is deliberately not here, because on the server it lives in checkin.py beside a live database and cannot be exercised without a bench. When that changes, add it.

distances.name: a point measured against itself is zero metres away
distances.why: The floor of the formula. A copy that returned anything else here would be wrong everywhere.

distances.name: a tenth of a degree of latitude is about eleven kilometres
distances.why: A degree of latitude is ~111 km everywhere on earth, so this pins the answer to a figure that does not come from any of the three implementations.

distances.name: a tenth of a degree of longitude is shorter than a tenth of latitude
distances.why: Meridians converge. At Kerala's latitude the difference is about 1.5%, which is small enough that a flat-earth copy would pass every other case here and fail this one.

distances.name: a hundred metres is a hundred metres
distances.why: The scale a radius is actually set at. A rounding error that does not matter over a kilometre decides whether somebody is refused at a gate.

distances.name: two ends of the earth do not break the formula
distances.why: Rounding can push the haversine term a hair above 1 for antipodal points, and asin of that is NaN — which propagates silently through every comparison downstream instead of raising.

coordinates.name: a coordinate that was never captured is not a place
coordinates.why: (0, 0) is in the Atlantic and is what an unset Float field reads as. Treating it as a place measures a punch against the Gulf of Guinea instead of refusing it honestly.

coordinates.name: a zero on one axis alone is still a place
coordinates.why: The equator and the Greenwich meridian are real. A rule that refused either would refuse it for everybody standing on one.

coordinates.name: a latitude off the map is not a place
coordinates.why: Beyond 90 the arithmetic still returns a number, and the number is meaningless.

coordinates.name: a longitude off the map is not a place
coordinates.why: Same again, at the other axis, where a wrapped value looks plausible.

coordinates.name: a real coordinate is a place
coordinates.why: The ordinary case, so that a copy which refused everything would fail rather than pass every negative test.
